breakfast.name: Jok (Thai Rice Porridge)
breakfast.description: Creamy rice porridge with pork or chicken, served with crispy fried shallots and soft-boiled eggs
ingredients: 1/4 lb ground pork or diced chicken
instructions: Bring broth to boil with ginger slices
Add rice and stir well
Reduce heat and simmer 20-25 minutes until rice breaks down
Rice should be very soft and porridge-like
Add ground pork and cook 5 minutes
Season with fish sauce and white pepper
Soft-boil eggs separately for 6 minutes
Ladle porridge into bowls
Top with soft-boiled egg, fried shallots, scallions, and cilantro
Serve with chili paste and lime
breakfast.notes: The consistency should be soupy, not thick. More broth can be added if needed
breakfast.fun_fact: Jok is considered Thai comfort food and soul food, eaten at any time of day

lunch.name: Pad Thai (Stir-Fried Noodles)
lunch.description: Rice noodles stir-fried with eggs, tofu, and shrimp in a tangy tamarind sauce
instructions: Soak rice noodles in room temperature water for 30 minutes until pliable
Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and palm sugar with 1/4 cup water
Heat oil in wok or large skillet over high heat
Add garlic and stir-fry 30 seconds
Push to side, crack eggs into pan and scramble lightly
Add shrimp or tofu, stir-fry until cooked
Add drained noodles and sauce, toss constantly for 2-3 minutes
Add half the bean sprouts and scallions
Toss and cook 1 more minute
Transfer to plate
Top with remaining bean sprouts, scallions, peanuts
Serve with lime wedges and dried chili
lunch.notes: Don't oversoak noodles or they'll be too soft. High heat and constant tossing are essential
lunch.fun_fact: Pad Thai became Thailand's national dish in the 1930s-40s as part of a nationalist campaign
alternatives: Brown sugar instead of palm sugar

dinner.name: Green Curry (Gaeng Keow Wan)
dinner.description: Aromatic green curry with chicken or shrimp in rich coconut broth with Thai herbs
ingredients: 1 cup green beans, cut into 2-inch pieces
instructions: Heat oil in large pan over medium heat
Add curry paste and fry for 1-2 minutes until fragrant
Add 1/2 can coconut milk, stir until paste dissolves
Add chicken and cook until just done
Add remaining coconut milk and bring to simmer
Add green beans, bell pepper, and eggplant
Simmer 8-10 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp
Add fish sauce and palm sugar
Adjust seasoning with lime juice
Stir in fresh basil
Serve hot with jasmine rice
dinner.notes: The green curry paste is the foundation - use quality brand for best results
dinner.fun_fact: Thai curries balance four key flavors: spicy (chili), salty (fish sauce), sweet (sugar), and sour (lime)
alternatives: Red curry paste for red curry

snacks.name: Spring Rolls (Cha Gio)
snacks.description: Crispy fried rolls filled with pork, shrimp, and vegetables, served with sweet-spicy dipping sauce
instructions: Make filling: Cook pork/shrimp until done, add garlic
Mix in cabbage, carrot, scallions, fish sauce, pepper
Cool filling completely
Dip rice paper in warm water for 5 seconds
Place on damp towel
Add 2 tbsp filling in center
Fold sides in, then roll tightly
Heat oil to 350°F
Deep fry rolls until golden and crispy (2-3 minutes)
Drain on paper towels
Serve hot with sweet chili sauce
snacks.notes: Rice paper should be pliable but not too wet or it tears
snacks.fun_fact: Spring rolls are popular appetizers at Thai restaurants and street vendors
alternatives: Spring roll wrappers instead of rice paper

desserts.name: Mango Sticky Rice (Khao Maeng Gai)
desserts.description: Sweet sticky rice served with fresh mango and coconut cream sauce
instructions: Cook sticky rice with water in rice cooker or pot
Once cooked, let sit in pot for 10 minutes
In small pot, heat coconut milk with palm sugar and salt
Stir until sugar dissolves
Pour warm coconut sauce over cooked rice
Stir gently to combine
Let sit 30 minutes to absorb sauce
Peel mangoes and slice into thick pieces
Arrange on plate with mound of sticky rice
Drizzle with coconut cream
Sprinkle with sesame seeds
Serve at room temperature
desserts.notes: Use ripe but firm mangoes. Over-ripe mangoes will be too soft
desserts.fun_fact: This is Thailand's most famous dessert, especially popular during mango season (March-May)
alternatives: Fresh passion fruit instead of mango

drinks.name: Thai Iced Tea (Cha Yen)
drinks.description: Sweet, creamy tea served cold with ice. Iconic Thai beverage with distinctive orange color
instructions: Boil water
Add Thai tea mix and steep 3-5 minutes
Strain through cheesecloth into pitcher
Cool to room temperature or chill
Fill glasses with ice
Pour cold tea, filling 3/4 way
Top with condensed milk
Add splash of evaporated milk for creaminess
Sprinkle sesame seeds on top
Stir and serve
drinks.notes: Thai tea mix is orange-colored and available in Asian markets
drinks.fun_fact: This sweet, creamy tea is ubiquitous at Thai restaurants and reflects Thai love of sweet beverages
alternatives: Use regular black tea with star anise and tamarind
Less milk for less sweet version
Coconut milk instead of evaporated milk

drinks.name: Chang Beer
drinks.description: Thailand's most popular beer, golden lager with crisp taste
instructions: Chill beer to 6-8°C
Pour into glass
Serve with ice or alongside Thai food
Traditionally served with a wedge of lime
drinks.notes: Best enjoyed ice-cold with Thai food
drinks.fun_fact: Chang means 'elephant' in Thai and is Thailand's most popular beer brand worldwide
